### Observed differences

- In the later window, A14 was not observed in any of the 200 traces (it previously ran in about 91 of 200, roughly 46 in 100), and A15 appeared in only 1 of 200 (previously about 109 of 200, 55 in 100); neither activity repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002]
- Before, A14 and A15 were strictly mutually exclusive alternatives that together covered every trace — no trace contained both, and none contained neither — while in the later window about 199 of 200 traces contain neither of them. [REL001, OCC001, OCC002]
- Routing around the dropped pair changed on all traces: A21's observed outgoing transitions, previously split between A22 (about 48 in 100), A15 (about 28) and A14 (about 25), now go to A22 in every trace, and A22's outgoing transitions, previously split between A23 (about 52), A15 (about 27) and A14 (about 21), now go to A23 in about 199 of 200 traces. [DIR003, DIR004]
- The surviving sequence tightened: A21 to A22 moved from one-or-two positions apart (about 48/52) to one position in all traces, A22 to A23 from one-or-two (about 52/48) to one position in about 995 of 1000, and A21 to A23 from three positions apart in all traces to two apart in about 995 of 1000. [LAG003, LAG005, LAG004]
- The earlier relations with A14 and A15 disappeared: A21 previously co-occurred with A14 (about 46 in 100 traces) and with A15 (about 55), always before them, and A14/A15 always preceded A23, with A22 falling before or after A14/A15 in roughly even splits; in the later window A21, A22 and A23 occur without A14/A15 in essentially all traces. [REL002, REL005, REL004, REL007, REL003, REL006]
- A23 still occurs in every trace; its mean relative position shifted slightly earlier (0.57 to 0.55), consistent with one fewer activity now sitting between A21 and A23. [POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative step between A21 and A23 — a choice between A14 and A15 — is no longer executed, so that in the later window traces run directly from A21 via A22 to A23. Previously every trace contained exactly one of A14 or A15 (about 46 versus 55 in 100) between A21 and A23; in the later window A14 is absent, A15 appears once, and A21, A22 and A23 still occur in all traces. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001, POS003]

The support is direct as well as consistent: the successor profiles of A21 and A22, measured on all 200 traces in both windows, lost their A14 and A15 components, and the A21–A23 distance shortened from three positions to two; because A14 and A15 each ran in roughly half of the earlier traces, their disappearance is unlikely to be a rare-variant sampling effect. [DIR003, DIR004, LAG004, OCC001, OCC002]

In total 21 evidence items qualified, many times the roughly 0.37 expected for an unchanged process, and each item's difference exceeds those of 199 of 200 random re-splits, so the overall volume and unusualness of the flagged behaviour cannot be explained by chance as a whole; most items, however, describe one underlying difference from different angles rather than independent changes. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

Limitations remain: zero participation only shows that A14 was not observed in the later window, and A15's single occurrence leaves open that it still executes very rarely, with the after-side profiles of the A15-specific items resting on that one trace. The evidence also cannot distinguish a removed branch from a choice that is simply never taken under current conditions, and while random re-splitting of a stable process cannot explain two activities falling from about 91 and 109 of 200 traces to 0 and 1, it could still account for the finer before-window splits. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, POS002, LAG001, LAG002, REL001]
